correctness.rationale: For all probability laws and zero-sum unit initial vectors the exact two-step expectation is x^T M2 x, with M2=Σ_ij p_i p_j P_i P_j P_i. Direct computation yields the reflection-even scalar and the reflection-odd two-by-two block. Averaging an arbitrary law with its reflection adds d²(P1−P3)², nonnegative and strictly positive in the unique top eigendirection at the interior symmetric law. Both boundary faces have loss one, above an interior candidate. Thus every minimizer is symmetric. The scalar f has f″≥3/2 using r=||(1−3a/2−a², a(10a+1)/4)||; endpoint derivative signs make its stationary point unique, and f′(3/10)<0 proves it differs from the global one-step optimum. The P3 characteristic polynomial strictly decreases in t=p(1−p), proving the minimal P4 boundary. verify.py reproduces rational matrix identities and the explicit rational root bracket; numerical checks are not used as infinite proofs.

originality.rationale: The closed radical and unique global minimizer for exact two-draw worst-initial-vector MSE on P4, its strict displacement from the uniquely optimal one-draw law, and the minimality statement for P2/P3 do not follow as stated from the closest inspected primary works. The 2014 exact-MSE tensor formula is general input to the problem, but the optimization there is the asymptotic annealed exponent; the 2004 gossip design solves the one-draw eigenvalue objective. Published nearby coordinate and two-row results concern different criteria. Several mathematical-formulation searches were actually completed; unknown unindexed small cases remain a disclosed risk.
residual_risks: A specialized unpublished, uncatalogued, or unindexed finite-two-step gossip probability design could reproduce the same P4 radical or optimizer.

value.rationale: Probability design in iid randomized projection/gossip algorithms is naturally motivated by both one-step guarantees and actual finite-horizon performance. The exact P4 minimax classification pinpoints the smallest connected path where those criteria choose different unique probability laws, converting a qualitative bound-versus-exact-error distinction into a theorem with explicit optimum, universal reduction over the full probability simplex and sharp transition. This structural boundary and reproducible formulas matter independently of the modest numerical gap. No claim of general horizon improvement or broader graph theorem is made.
